meta.title: Source Library
meta.description: The evidentiary base of the record: courts, UN bodies, human rights organisations, peer-reviewed research, open datasets, declassified archives and the Israeli press. Sources are grouped by the weight they carry, not by convenience. Every claim in the report is anchored to a source of one of these classes.
meta.note: Where a link is given it points to the authoritative publisher, not to an aggregator. Where no link is given the source is a print or archival record cited in the report's bibliography.

groups.label: Courts and tribunals
groups.blurb: Judgments, orders and advisory opinions. The highest evidentiary class in this record: findings of fact and law by the bodies competent to make them. Domestic judgments are listed here only where a question raised in this record has actually been litigated to judgment in a national court.

items.title: Legal Consequences of the Construction of a Wall in the Occupied Palestinian Territory
items.note: Advisory Opinion. Held the wall and the settlement enterprise contrary to international law and affirmed the applicability of the Fourth Geneva Convention to the occupied territory.

items.title: Application of the Genocide Convention (South Africa v. Israel) — Order on Provisional Measures
items.note: Found it plausible that the acts complained of fall within the Genocide Convention; ordered Israel to prevent and punish direct and public incitement to genocide. Measures strengthened 28 March and 24 May 2024.

items.title: Legal Consequences arising from the Policies and Practices of Israel in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem
items.note: Advisory Opinion. The occupation is unlawful and must end as rapidly as possible; settlements must be dismantled; reparations paid. Paragraph 229 found a breach of Article 3 CERD (racial segregation and apartheid).

items.title: Arrest warrants against Benjamin Netanyahu and Yoav Gallant
items.org: International Criminal Court, Pre-Trial Chamber I
items.note: Reasonable grounds to believe both bear responsibility for the war crime of starvation as a method of warfare and crimes against humanity of murder, persecution and other inhumane acts. A warrant was also issued against Hamas commander Mohammed Deif.

items.title: Situation in the State of Palestine
items.org: International Criminal Court, Office of the Prosecutor
items.note: The open investigation covering conduct in the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza since 13 June 2014.

items.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina v. Serbia and Montenegro
items.note: The only ICJ ruling directly on the duty to prevent genocide. The obligation arises the moment a state learns of a serious risk, not once genocide is proven; it is a duty of conduct, and it is irrelevant whether full effort would have succeeded.

items.title: Prosecutor v. Akayesu (ICTR-96-4-T)
items.note: The foundational jurisprudence on inferring genocidal intent from a pattern of conduct and from dehumanising speech.

items.title: University of Bristol v Dr David Miller [2026] EAT 84
items.note: Appeal EA-2024-000324-RS. Lord Fairley KC, with Nick Aziz and Dr Gillian Smith MBE. Eight of nine grounds rejected; anti-Zionist belief in the formulation advanced held a protected philosophical belief, dismissal held direct discrimination. Compensation reduced by 50 per cent for contributory conduct.

groups.label: United Nations bodies
groups.blurb: Commissions of inquiry, treaty bodies, special procedures and operational agencies. Mandated, methodologically documented, and published under institutional accountability.

items.title: Report of the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the OPT (A/HRC/60/CRP.3)
items.note: The first UN body to find that Israel has committed genocide in Gaza, and that Herzog, Netanyahu and Gallant incited it. Chair: Navi Pillay.

items.title: Report of the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the OPT
items.note: Second affirmative genocide finding, on the deliberate targeting of children. Chair: Srinivasan Muralidhar.

items.title: Anatomy of a Genocide (A/HRC/55/73)
items.org: UN Special Rapporteur on the OPT, Francesca Albanese
items.note: The first UN mandate-holder report to conclude that the threshold indicating genocide had been met.

items.title: Report on starvation and the right to food in Gaza
items.org: UN Special Rapporteur on the Right to Food, Michael Fakhri
items.note: Concluded that Israel was committing genocide by starvation.

items.title: Forcible displacement in the northern West Bank refugee camps
items.note: Found the displacement of 33,000+ Palestinians from Jenin, Nur Shams and Tulkarem during Operation Iron Wall to be large-scale, long-term and systematic, raising concerns of the crime against humanity of forcible transfer.

items.title: Report of the Special Committee to Investigate Israeli Practices
items.note: Found Israel's warfare methods in Gaza consistent with genocide, including the use of starvation as a weapon.

items.title: Humanitarian situation updates, occupied Palestinian territory
items.org: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
items.note: The operational casualty, displacement and access record. OCHA's verified fatality database covers 2008–2023; the post-October-2023 figures appear in situation updates pending full verification.

items.title: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification — Gaza analyses
items.note: The authoritative famine classification, including the confirmation of Famine (IPC Phase 5) conditions in Gaza governorates.

items.title: Health system attacks and casualty reporting, oPt
items.note: The Surveillance System for Attacks on Health Care (SSA) record, and WHO's independent assessment of Ministry of Health casualty data.

items.title: Situation reports, occupied Palestinian territory
items.note: Displacement, shelter and staff-casualty data, and the record of the funding and legislative campaign against the agency.

items.title: Damage assessments, Gaza Strip
items.note: Satellite-derived building damage assessments — the independent physical corroboration of the destruction figures.

items.title: Child casualty and grave-violations reporting
items.note: Including the Secretary-General's annual Children and Armed Conflict report, which listed Israeli forces for grave violations against children in June 2024.

items.title: Report of the UN Fact-Finding Mission on the Gaza Conflict (the Goldstone Report, A/HRC/12/48)
items.note: Documented the Dahiya Doctrine of deliberate disproportionality as policy rather than error.

items.title: Database of business enterprises involved in activities relating to Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territory
items.org: UN Human Rights Office (OHCHR), mandated by HRC resolution 31/36
items.date: first published February 2020; updated June 2023 and July 2025
items.note: The only United Nations register of named companies with settlement-linked operations. The listing grew from 112 enterprises in 2020 to 158 in July 2025. It records listed activity, not a legal finding against any company.

items.title: Resolution 181 (II): Future Government of Palestine (the Partition Plan)
items.note: The territorial allocation against which every later land figure is measured: 56 per cent of Mandatory Palestine to a Jewish state, 43 per cent to an Arab state, Jerusalem under international administration.

items.title: “The essence of childhood has been destroyed”: Israel's deliberate targeting of Palestinian children in the Occupied Palestinian Territory since 7 October 2023
items.org: UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the OPT
items.note: Report A/HRC/62/CRP.2. Found the deliberate targeting of Palestinian children amounting to genocide and atrocity crimes in Gaza and war crimes in the West Bank, covering 7 October 2023 to 31 March 2026: at least 20,179 children killed and 44,143 injured.

items.title: Israel's discriminatory death penalty law marks grave human rights retrogression, UN anti-racism committee warns
items.org: UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination / OHCHR
items.note: Finds the Death Penalty for Terrorists Law racially discriminatory and an instance of segregation, applying de facto to Palestinians only, and calls on all States parties to ensure their resources are not used to enforce discriminatory policies.

items.title: Israel's death penalty law constitutes discriminatory regime of capital punishment: UN experts
items.note: Special Rapporteur on torture Alice Jill Edwards and others on hanging, the 90-day execution deadline and the prohibition on mandatory death sentences under the ICCPR.

groups.label: Human rights organisations
groups.blurb: Investigations with documented methodology by the organisations with the longest field presence. Israeli and Palestinian organisations are listed alongside the international ones because their findings converge.

items.title: A Threshold Crossed: Israeli Authorities and the Crimes of Apartheid and Persecution
items.note: The first apartheid finding by a major international organisation.

items.title: Extermination and Acts of Genocide: Israel Deliberately Depriving Palestinians in Gaza of Water
items.note: The genocide determination on water deprivation grounds.

items.title: Israel's Apartheid Against Palestinians: Cruel System of Domination and Crime Against Humanity
items.note: 278 pages compiled over four years.

items.title: 'You Feel Like You Are Subhuman': Israel's Genocide Against Palestinians in Gaza
items.note: Amnesty's affirmative genocide determination.

items.title: Erasing Anything Palestinian
items.note: Found a state-led campaign of ethnic cleansing in the West Bank and named Netanyahu, Ben-Gvir, Katz, Smotrich and Strock.

items.title: This is Apartheid: A Regime of Jewish Supremacy from the Jordan River to the Mediterranean Sea
items.note: The Israeli organisation's apartheid finding, covering all territory under Israeli control.

items.title: Our Genocide
items.note: B'Tselem's genocide determination, published simultaneously with Physicians for Human Rights Israel's.

items.title: Statistics on Palestinians and Israelis killed
items.note: The longest continuous independently maintained fatality database for the occupied territories, with per-person records.

items.title: Genocide in Gaza — the destruction of the health system
items.note: The medical profession's genocide finding, from inside Israeli civil society.

items.title: The Perimeter: Soldiers' testimonies from the Gaza Buffer Zone 2023–2024
items.note: Dozens of IDF testimonies documenting the razing of roughly 16% of the Gaza Strip to create a kill zone at least a kilometre deep.

items.title: Law enforcement on Israeli civilians in the West Bank — data sheets
items.note: Two decades of Israeli police file outcomes: over 93% of settler-violence investigations closed without indictment.

items.title: Legal analyses and submissions on the occupation, apartheid and genocide
items.note: The oldest Palestinian human rights organisation (founded 1979), an ICJ and ICC intervenor.

items.title: Field documentation and casualty investigations, Gaza
items.org: Al Mezan Center for Human Rights
items.note: Gaza-based field documentation of individual incidents.

items.title: Casualty and detention documentation
items.note: Weekly documented reporting from Gaza since 1995.

items.title: Child fatality and detention monitoring
items.note: The specialist record on child killings, arrest and military detention.

items.title: Verified statement and incident documentation
items.note: Independent verification and cataloguing of the most probative ministerial and military statements.

items.title: Field reporting from Gaza's hospitals
items.note: MSF has independently described the conduct in Gaza as genocide.

items.title: Reports on Gaza and the occupied territory
items.note: Including the water and aid-access analyses underpinning the starvation findings.

items.title: Reports on settlement expansion
items.note: The Israeli monitoring project on settlement construction, outposts and land seizure.

items.title: Statistics on Palestinian political prisoners and administrative detention
items.org: Addameer Prisoner Support and Human Rights Association
items.note: The cumulative record of detention under Israeli military order: more than 800,000 Palestinians detained since 1967, roughly 20% of the population of the occupied territory.

items.title: Statistics on house demolitions in the occupied territories
items.note: Compiled from the Israeli Ministry of Interior, the Jerusalem Municipality, the Civil Administration, OCHA and field work: roughly 52,000 homes demolished in the Nakba and more than 55,000 structures in the occupied territory since 1967.

items.title: Home demolitions in East Jerusalem, 1967–2018
items.note: 5,000 homes demolished since 1967, of which 1,706 between 2000 and 2017, displacing 9,422 people including 5,443 children.

items.title: Exclusion and observation decisions, Government Pension Fund Global
items.org: Norges Bank Investment Management, on the advice of the Council on Ethics
items.note: The world's largest sovereign wealth fund, and the most closely watched single test of the settlement-business listings. Source for the divestment record, alongside KLP, PFZW and AkademikerPension.

items.title: Corporate involvement in the occupation — company database
items.note: Independent Israeli research centre documenting the commercial infrastructure of the occupation, settlement industry and control of the Palestinian population. Predates and feeds the OHCHR database.

items.title: Israel Passes Mandatory Death Penalty for Palestinians Convicted of Terrorism
items.note: Provisions, the 96 per cent military-court conviction rate recorded by B'Tselem, and the reactions of the Council of Europe, Human Rights Watch and the US State Department.

items.title: Genocide Watch Gaza Report, July 2026
items.note: Places Gaza simultaneously at Stages 8 (persecution), 9 (extermination) and 10 (denial) of Gregory Stanton's ten-stage model, and addresses Hamas's attacks on Israeli civilians in the same report.

items.title: CPJ, partners file emergency motion to Israeli Supreme Court seeking independent media access to Gaza
items.note: Filed with the Foreign Press Association, Reporters Without Borders and the Union of Journalists in Israel. Records the ban on independent international press access to Gaza at more than 900 days.

items.title: RSF appeals to Israeli Supreme Court against the media blackout imposed on Gaza
items.note: The petition record on foreign press access, including the seven deferrals granted to the state in the petition's first year.

items.title: US Sanctions ICC President Tomoko Akane
items.note: Records the 18 August 2026 designations of the Court's President and a senior trial lawyer, bringing the total to nine of eighteen judges, both Deputy Prosecutors and the former Prosecutor.

items.title: Internal Fight: Palestinian Abuses in Gaza and the West Bank
items.note: Record of the 2007 factional killings, finding that more Palestinians died in internal Palestinian fighting that year (at least 490) than from Israeli attacks (at least 396), and that both Hamas and Fatah forces committed summary executions and torture (§18.10).

items.title: 'Strangling Necks': Abductions, torture and summary killings of Palestinians by Hamas forces during the 2014 Gaza/Israel conflict
items.note: Documents the extrajudicial execution of at least 23 Palestinians by Hamas forces during the 2014 conflict, including six men publicly executed outside the al-Omari mosque on 22 August 2014 (§18.10).

items.title: "Two Authorities, One Way, Zero Dissent": Arbitrary Arrest and Torture Under the Palestinian Authority and Hamas
items.note: Two-year investigation across 86 cases and 147 interviews finding that torture practised by both the Palestinian Authority and Hamas may amount to a crime against humanity (§18.10).

groups.label: Statement and incitement databases
groups.blurb: Structured, continuously updated registers of the statement record. Both compile from publicly available primary sources and leave the legal determination to the courts.

items.title: Database with 500+ Instances of Israeli Incitement to Genocide
items.note: Categorised by genocidal intent, forced displacement and collective punishment; much of the evidence originates from the President, Prime Minister, Knesset members, military personnel and law enforcement.

items.title: A Registry of Israeli Genocidal Statements on Gaza
items.note: Over 1,000 documented instances of incitement and genocidal intent since 7 October 2023.

items.title: Red Flag Alerts and statements on incitement
items.note: Including the Red Flag Alert on Israel in Lebanon (March 2026) and the statement on Ben-Gvir's incitement (1 September 2026).

items.title: Ten Stages of Genocide assessments — Gaza
items.note: Assessed Gaza at Stages 8 (Persecution), 9 (Extermination) and 10 (Denial) simultaneously.

items.title: Statements by Israeli Officials, Soldiers and Civil Society on Genocide
items.note: Compilation of official and informal translations, each with the Hebrew original and a link to the recording or post it was taken from. Assembled as the genocide case was filed at the International Court of Justice.

groups.label: Open datasets
groups.blurb: Machine-readable series used to build the charts in this dashboard. Where a series is aggregated or interpolated, the chart note says so.

items.title: Palestine Datasets — daily casualties, named martyrs, press casualties, infrastructure damage
items.note: Public-domain aggregation of Gaza Ministry of Health, Government Media Office and West Bank figures. The source of the monthly and cumulative series on the Data view.

items.title: palestine-datasets (source repository)
items.note: Build pipeline, schemas and caveats on completeness for the datasets above.

items.title: Data on casualties
items.note: The verified fatality database covering 2008 onward. Published through an interactive dashboard rather than a public API, so pre-2023 annual figures in this record are cited individually.

items.title: Fatalities database
items.note: Per-person records with date, location, age, and the circumstances of each killing.

items.title: Israel–Palestine conflict event data
items.org: ACLED (Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project)
items.note: Geolocated event-level data used for cross-checking incident counts and locations.

items.title: Civilian harm assessments, Israel and Palestine
items.note: Incident-by-incident open-source assessment of civilian harm from specific strikes.

items.title: Journalist casualty database
items.note: The independent count of journalists and media workers killed.

items.title: Gaza damage proxy maps
items.org: Corey Scher (CUNY) and Jamon Van Den Hoek (Oregon State University)
items.note: Synthetic-aperture-radar damage proxy mapping, the independent academic corroboration of UNOSAT's assessments.

items.title: Palestinians killed since 1948 — World Refugee Day statistical release
items.note: The only cumulative figure published by the Palestinian statistical authority: 136,000 Palestinians killed since 1948. The period-by-period basis has not been published.

items.title: Arms Transfers Database and Trends in International Arms Transfers, 2024
items.note: The standard open register of state-to-state major-weapons transfers. Source for the supplier shares used in the complicity ledger: 66 per cent of Israeli major arms imports in 2020–2024 from the United States and 33 per cent from Germany.

items.title: Security Council — Veto List (Quick Links)
items.note: The complete record of vetoes cast in the Security Council since 1946, by member and by draft resolution. Source for the veto wall: 49 United States vetoes of draft resolutions concerning Israel and Palestine, the largest single-subject block in the Council's history.

groups.label: Peer-reviewed research
groups.blurb: Published, methodologically transparent research — principally on mortality estimation, where the difference between recorded and actual death tolls is the central empirical question.

items.title: Traumatic injury mortality in the Gaza Strip from Oct 7, 2023, to June 30, 2024: a capture–recapture analysis
items.note: Estimated the Ministry of Health count under-reported traumatic-injury deaths by approximately 41% over the period studied.

items.title: Gaza Mortality Survey
items.note: Household-survey estimate of roughly 75,200 violent deaths plus 16,300 non-violent excess deaths, implying an undercount of about 35% and some 12,200 missing.

items.title: Estimates of Gaza mortality and life expectancy
items.org: Max Planck Institute for Demographic Research (MPIDR)
items.note: Independent demographic reconstruction of the death toll and of the collapse in life expectancy.

items.title: Costs of War Project — Gaza
items.note: Source of the widely cited 186,000 figure, which applies an indirect-to-direct death multiplier; it is a projection of total war-attributable mortality, not a body count, and is presented as such in this record.

items.title: Bad News From Israel and More Bad News From Israel
items.org: Glasgow University Media Group (Greg Philo and Mike Berry)
items.note: The foundational audience and content studies on Western media coverage of the conflict.

items.title: The Hundred Years' War on Palestine
items.note: Documents the Zionist movement's own institutional use of the vocabulary of colonisation.

items.title: The Ethnic Cleansing of Palestine
items.note: Archive-based account of Plan Dalet and the 1948 expulsions.

items.title: The Birth of the Palestinian Refugee Problem Revisited
items.note: The most detailed documentary reconstruction of the 1948 expulsions, by a historian who rejects the ethnic-cleansing framing — cited here for the facts, not the interpretation.

items.title: Zionism in the Age of the Dictators
items.note: Source for the Haavara Agreement and Kareski affair material, corroborated against Institute for Palestine Studies and German Foreign Ministry archive records.

items.title: U.S. Foreign Aid to Israel (RL33222) and successive In Focus briefs
items.org: Congressional Research Service, Library of Congress
items.note: Congress's own non-partisan accounting of cumulative and annual United States assistance to Israel: $150bn cumulative as of February 2022, $158.7bn as of March 2023, and the current figure of roughly $174bn in nominal terms.

items.title: United States Spending on Israel's Military Operations and Related U.S. Operations in the Region
items.org: Costs of War Project, Watson Institute, Brown University
items.note: Independent costing of the first year of the war: $17.9bn in direct military assistance to Israel plus $4.86bn in related United States regional operations, and $317.9bn cumulative since 1959 once adjusted for inflation.

items.title: Jews Against Zionism: The American Council for Judaism, 1942–1948
items.org: Thomas A. Kolsky, Temple University Press
items.note: The standard scholarly history of organised American Jewish opposition to the establishment of a Jewish state. Cited at §23.2.

items.title: Genocide in Gaza: Israel’s Long War on Palestine
items.note: Essays written between 2009 and 2024 by the Oxford emeritus professor and former Israeli soldier, applying both the apartheid and the genocide characterisations. Cited at §23.3.

items.title: Israeli state terrorism: knowledge, power and the “public secret”
items.org: Richard Jackson, Critical Studies on Terrorism
items.note: Argues that Israeli state terrorism is extensively documented yet unacknowledged in terrorism and security studies, including critical terrorism studies itself.

items.title: Why we need to talk about 'state terrorism' by Israel in Gaza
items.org: Richard Jackson and Mandy Turner, Security in Context
items.note: Applies the audience-directed definition of terrorism to the Gaza campaign and argues the label is withheld selectively from Western states and their allies.

items.title: The Ghosts of State Terror: Knowledge, Politics and Terrorism Studies
items.org: Richard Jackson, Critical Studies on Terrorism 1(3)
items.note: The standard account of why terrorism studies defines terrorism in actor-based terms that exclude states, and the case against doing so.

items.title: State Terrorism in the Social Sciences: Theories, Methods and Concepts
items.org: Ruth Blakeley, in Jackson, Murphy and Poynting (eds), Contemporary State Terrorism
items.note: The four-element definition of state terrorism relied on at Part XXIV: a deliberate act or threat of violence by state agents, against victims, directed at a wider audience, for political ends.

items.title: Anonymous Soldiers: The Struggle for Israel, 1917-1947
items.note: The standard history of the Irgun and Lehi campaigns, built on the British archives opened in the 2000s, by the terrorism scholar whose work is foundational to the field. Records that the groups “were called terrorists by the Jews in Palestine, by the British, and by the press”. Endorsed by Benny Morris as “the best comprehensive study of the Jewish extremists' terror/guerrilla campaign against the British in Palestine”.

items.title: The Growing Rift between Holocaust Scholars over Israel/Palestine
items.note: Analysis of the split within Holocaust studies over Gaza, tracing it to competing positions on the uniqueness of the Holocaust. Cited at §24.2A for the dissenting position stated in its own terms.

groups.label: Israeli sources
groups.blurb: Israeli journalism, official statements and leaked internal material. Under this record's evidentiary rule, admissions by the state and its press carry the greatest weight against the state.

items.title: Investigative reporting on Gaza and the West Bank
items.note: Including the human-shields investigation (13 August 2024), the leaked Maj. Gen. Bluth briefing (4 May 2026), the Geocartography/Penn State polling (March 2025), and Ehud Olmert's ethnic-cleansing columns (June 2026). Includes the magazine feature of 9 September 2026 carrying an Israeli Air Force drone operator's account of fire directed at rescue vehicles and at medical personnel sheltering behind ambulances (§14.1B).

items.title: +972 Magazine
items.note: Including the 'Lavender' and 'Where's Daddy?' investigations into AI-assisted targeting, sourced to serving Israeli intelligence officers.

items.title: Local Call (Sicha Mekomit)
items.note: The Hebrew-language partner publication to +972, and the route by which several investigations first appeared in Hebrew.

items.title: Liveblog and daily reporting
items.note: The most complete English-language record of ministerial statements, Knesset proceedings and IDF announcements.

items.title: Broadcast investigations and leaks
items.note: Publisher of the leaked Haliva briefing recording (August 2025) and the police command-room footage from 7 October (February 2026).

items.title: Ynet / Yedioth Ahronoth
items.note: Including the Katz depopulation remarks at the Ynet conference (September 2026) and the 1983 Eitan interview.

items.title: Knesset records and Ethics Committee decisions
items.note: Including the February 2025 Ethics Committee ruling that calling Palestinians 'subhumans' and calling to 'kill all adult men' did not violate Knesset ethical standards.

items.title: Official statements and orders
items.org: Israeli Ministry of Defence and the IDF Spokesperson's Unit
items.note: The primary record for the siege orders of October 2023 and subsequent operational announcements.

items.title: Prosecution of soldiers for offences against Palestinians — data sheets
items.org: Yesh Din — Volunteers for Human Rights
items.note: The military-justice funnel, from Israeli military records: 2,427 complaints between 2016 and 2024 produced 552 investigations (22.7%) and 23 indictments (0.9%). Yesh Din puts the probability of prosecution for killing a Palestinian at 0.4%.

items.title: Attacks on Christians in Israel and East Jerusalem: Annual Report 2025
items.org: Rossing Center for Education and Dialogue
items.note: Third annual report of the Israeli organisation's Jerusalem Center for Jewish-Christian Relations. 155 documented incidents in 2025 against 111 in 2024 and 89 in 2023, with 61 physical assaults and 52 attacks on church property.

items.title: Israel should ‘wipe out’ Palestinian town of Huwara, says senior minister Smotrich
items.note: The verbatim remark by the Finance Minister and minister responsible for civil administration in the occupied West Bank, five days after the settler attack on the town (§9.2A).

groups.label: Investigative journalism
groups.blurb: International investigations that established facts not otherwise in the public record.

items.title: Reporting on Gaza, the occupation and UK complicity
items.note: Including the joint investigations with +972 and Local Call on AI-assisted targeting and the secret systems reporting, and the interview of 13 July 2025 in which Ehud Olmert called the planned Rafah “humanitarian city” a concentration camp (§6.3A).

items.title: Investigations into UK military support
items.note: Source, with Action on Armed Violence, of the record of 600+ RAF surveillance flights over Gaza (December 2023 – October 2025).

items.title: Reporting on arms transfers and civilian harm
items.note: Including the call for UK sanctions on Moshe Feiglin over the May 2025 remarks on Gaza's children.

items.title: Daily coverage and verification
items.note: The most continuous on-the-ground reporting from Gaza; its Sanad verification unit is cited throughout the record.

items.title: Middle East Eye
items.note: Source for several Knesset-floor statements, including the Waldiger exchange of 13 May 2025, and for the Israeli government document of 8 September 2019 recording UK Lawyers for Israel's request to the Justice Ministry for assistance (§13.9).

items.title: Wire reporting
items.note: Used for cross-corroboration: this record requires at least two independent sources for every new statistic.

items.title: Reporting on UK politics and the Middle East
items.note: Source of the report of 13 September 2026 that UK Lawyers for Israel had written to Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood urging the proscription of Médecins Sans Frontières under the Terrorism Act 2000 (§13.9).

items.title: Reporting on the Arab world and Palestine
items.note: Carried Médecins Sans Frontières' response to the proscription demand verbatim, together with the reaction of former British Army general Charlie Herbert (§13.9).

items.title: Mehdi Unfiltered and reporting on Gaza
items.note: Source of the debate of 9 September 2026 between Peter Beinart and Joel Rubin, moderated by Mehdi Hasan, on where criticism of Israel ends and antisemitism begins (§21.8).

items.title: In the Shadow of the Holocaust
items.note: The essay describing Gaza as a ghetto, on which the Heinrich Böll Foundation withdrew from awarding the Hannah Arendt Prize. Cited at §23.3.

items.title: We need an exodus from Zionism
items.note: The full text of the Passover address at the Jewish Voice for Peace “Seder in the Streets”, Brooklyn, 23 April 2024. Cited at §23.4.

items.title: Israeli minister threatens to revoke filmmakers' citizenship over Gaza film
items.note: Culture Minister Miki Zohar and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir on the directors of NAZA after its Venice Special Jury Prize, with the legal position on citizenship revocation.

items.title: IDF rejects testimonies in Israeli-made documentary about AI-powered killing in Gaza
items.note: The IDF Spokesperson's Unit's rebuttal in full: the testimonies are anonymous and unverifiable, they include claims of strategy beyond junior soldiers' knowledge, and strike decisions are made by human personnel only.

items.title: Transcript: Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan
items.note: The United States' own gloss on Point 19 of the twenty-point plan: statehood only through a negotiated deal with Israel, no recognition now, "we are far from that", and the closing note that Trump still opposes West Bank annexation.

items.title: Read Trump's 20-point proposal to end the war in Gaza
items.note: Full text of the plan endorsed by UN Security Council Resolution 2803, including Point 19 on a credible pathway to Palestinian self-determination and statehood and Point 20 on a political horizon.

items.title: US sanctions 'Hilltop Youth', treating extreme settler activists as an organized group
items.org: The Times of Israel / US Department of the Treasury (OFAC), Executive Order 14115
items.note: The designation describes a campaign of killings, arson, assault and intimidation intended to drive Palestinian communities out of the West Bank. Executive Order 14115 was revoked on 20 January 2025 and the designations lifted by OFAC on 24 January 2025.

items.title: Leading Israeli Scholar Avi Shlaim: Israel Committing “State Terror” in Gaza Attack
items.note: Shlaim defines terror as “the use of violence against civilians for political purposes” and applies the definition to Hamas and to Israel in the same answer. The symmetry is his own method, and it is the method applied at Part XVIII and Part XXIV.

items.title: Supreme Court rejects appeal by Israeli killer of Palestinian family in arson attack
items.note: Reports the dismissal of Amiram Ben-Uliel's appeal against conviction for the Duma arson of 31 July 2015, an offence classified by the Lod District Court as a terrorist act.

items.title: Bigoted Harassment of Christians in Jerusalem Increased in 2025
items.note: Sets the Rossing Center 2025 figures alongside the Religious Freedom Data Center's independent count of 181 incidents, 109 of them spitting, with 43 in the Armenian Quarter.

items.title: Report shows rise in attacks on Christians in Israel, but a willingness to tackle issue
items.note: The 2024 Rossing Center report and its accompanying survey, including the emigration figures and Hana Bendcowsky's remarks on reporting and on police practice.

items.title: Macklemore Dropped From Ed Sheeran Tour After Onstage ‘Free Palestine’ Statements
items.note: Jon Blistein. Carries Messina Touring Group's exclusive statement and names the seven stadiums reported as refusing to host the tour with Macklemore on the bill.

items.title: Statement on removal from The Loop tour
items.note: Twelve-panel statement published on the artist's own accounts. Sets out his account of the removal, including conversations he attributes to Ed Sheeran, and argues that there is no neutral position between the oppressor and the oppressed. The passages describing private conversations are his assertions and are recorded as such.

items.title: How Israel Helped to Spawn Hamas
items.note: The investigation carrying the statement of Avner Cohen, the Israeli official responsible for religious affairs in Gaza for more than two decades, that "Hamas, to my great regret, is Israel’s creation", and the record of the military administration’s registration of Sheikh Ahmed Yassin’s Mujama al-Islamiya as a charity in 1977 (§11.1). The wider "Israel created Hamas" shorthand is contested and is recorded in the report only at the strength the evidence supports.

items.title: Huwara: The settler attack on this West Bank town was called a ‘pogrom’ by Israel’s military. Videos show soldiers did little to stop it
items.note: Months-long video investigation, with testimony gathered by Breaking the Silence, finding that Israeli soldiers present during the 26 February 2023 attack on Huwara did not intervene and that fire engines and ambulances were held back (§9.2A).

items.title: Before They Vowed to Annihilate Hamas, Israeli Officials Considered It an Asset
items.note: Source for Bezalel Smotrich’s October 2015 formulation, "The Palestinian Authority is a burden, and Hamas is an asset", and for the stated reasoning about recognition, the International Criminal Court and the Security Council (§11.1).

groups.label: Declassified and primary archives
groups.blurb: Contemporaneous documents rather than later accounts of them.

items.title: Ben-Gurion diaries and the 1937 Ben-Gurion letter
items.note: Primary source for the transfer material of 1937, including the diary entry of 12 July 1937.

items.title: Jewish Agency Executive minutes
items.note: Including the 29 October 1936 transfer proposal and Arthur Ruppin's 1938 remarks on the transfer of entire villages.

items.title: Mandate-era files on Zionist paramilitary organisations
items.org: The National Archives, Kew (British MI5 and Colonial Office)
items.note: The British designation of the Irgun and Lehi as terrorist organisations, and the contemporaneous assessments.

items.title: Haavara Agreement records
items.note: The documentary record of the transfer agreement and associated correspondence.

items.title: Israel State Archives
items.note: Declassified cabinet protocols, including the 1970 protocols on self-determination for the West Bank population.

items.title: Der Judenstaat (The Jewish State)
items.note: The founding pamphlet of political Zionism, in the 1946 American Zionist Emergency Council English text. The German original is Project Gutenberg ebook 28865.

items.title: 'The Iron Wall (We and the Arabs)'
items.note: The statement that Zionist settlement could proceed only behind a wall of force the Arab population could not break, written by the founder of Revisionist Zionism.

items.title: 'Truth from Eretz Yisrael'
items.note: The early Zionist thinker's account of how the existing Arab population was being treated by the first settlers, published after his visit of 1891.

items.title: J50 Declaration on Zionism and Antisemitism
items.org: J50 Forum, published by the European Jewish Congress
items.note: Primary text and full signatory list: seven global and regional organisations and fifty-two national and community organisations across forty countries. Reaffirms the IHRA working definition and declares anti-Zionism, as defined in the operative paragraph, antisemitic. Creates no legal obligation.

items.title: The Pittsburgh Platform (1885) and the rabbinic response to the First Zionist Congress (1897)
items.note: The founding statement of American Reform Judaism and the CCAR and UAHC resolutions opposing the establishment of a Jewish state. Cited at §1.0 and §23.2.

items.title: Document: Shamir on Terrorism (1943)
items.org: MERIP (Middle East Research and Information Project)
items.note: Translation of the article “Terror” from the Lehi journal HeHazit, summer 1943, attributed to Yitzhak Yezernitzky (later Prime Minister Yitzhak Shamir). Translations of the passage vary and some sources attribute the article to the journal without naming an author.

groups.label: Legal instruments
groups.blurb: The treaty and statutory texts against which the conduct in this record is assessed.

items.title: Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide
items.note: Article II (acts and specific intent); Article III(c) (direct and public incitement).

items.title: Geneva Convention (IV) relative to the Protection of Civilian Persons in Time of War
items.org: International Committee of the Red Cross
items.note: Article 33 (collective punishment); Article 49 (deportation, forcible transfer, and transfer of the occupier's own population into occupied territory).

items.title: Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court
items.note: Article 7 (crimes against humanity, including apartheid and forcible transfer); Article 8 (war crimes, including starvation as a method of warfare).

items.title: International Convention on the Suppression and Punishment of the Crime of Apartheid
items.note: The standalone definition of apartheid as a crime against humanity, independent of the South African case.

items.title: International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (CERD)
items.note: Article 3, on racial segregation and apartheid — the provision the ICJ found Israel to have breached on 19 July 2024.

items.title: Basic Law: Israel — the Nation State of the Jewish People
items.note: Cited by B'Tselem and Adalah as constitutional confirmation that the distinction between Jews and non-Jews is treated as fundamental.

items.title: Israeli–Palestinian Interim Agreement on the West Bank and the Gaza Strip (Oslo II), Annex I
items.org: Signed at Washington, D.C.; deposited with the United Nations
items.note: The instrument that created Areas A, B and C as a five-year interim arrangement. Thirty-one years on, Area C — 60 per cent of the West Bank, holding every settlement, the Jordan Valley and the aquifers — remains under full Israeli control.

items.title: Absentees' Property Law, 5710–1950; Development Authority (Transfer of Property) Law, 5710–1950; Land Acquisition (Validation of Acts and Compensation) Law, 5713–1953
items.note: The statutory machinery by which property left by Palestinian refugees was vested in the Custodian of Absentee Property and transferred onward to the state. Applied in East Jerusalem after 1967 and upheld, with restrictions, by the Israeli Supreme Court in 2015.

items.title: Equality Act 2010
items.note: Section 10 (religion or belief as a protected characteristic); section 13 (direct discrimination). The provisions under which an anti-Zionist belief was held protected in Miller.

items.title: Administrative Appeal 8277/17, Zayoud v. Minister of the Interior
items.note: An expanded seven-justice panel upheld the constitutionality of Article 11(b)(2) of the Citizenship Law, 5712-1952, which allows a court for administrative affairs to revoke citizenship for a breach of loyalty on the Interior Minister's application, even where the result is statelessness. The qualifying acts are enumerated as terrorism, treason or serious espionage, and the acquisition of status in a hostile state.

items.title: R (Huda Ammori) v Secretary of State for the Home Department [2026] EWHC 292 (Admin)
items.org: Divisional Court of the King's Bench Division, England and Wales
items.note: Proscription of Palestine Action held to be outside the Home Secretary's own policy and a disproportionate interference with Articles 10 and 11 ECHR; reversed by the Court of Appeal, [2026] EWCA Civ 1721, 15 June 2026, with permission to appeal granted by the Supreme Court in July 2026.

items.title: Executive Order 14203, "Imposing Sanctions on the International Criminal Court"
items.note: The instrument under which the Prosecutor, nine judges, both Deputy Prosecutors, Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese and three Palestinian human rights organisations have been designated.

items.title: The ICC strongly rejects new US sanctions designations
items.note: The Court's own response, describing the measures as a flagrant attack against the independence of an impartial judicial institution.
